text: The Nike Cortez is the first running shoe released by Nike in 1972 and is considered a significant factor in the company's success. It was designed by Nike co-founders Bill Bowerman and Phil Knight, who first met in 1957 when Knight competed on Bowerman's track team at the University of Oregon. Knight acquired the distribution rights for Onitsuka Tiger athletic shoes in the U.S., and the two founded Blue Ribbon Sports, which later changed its name to Nike in 1972. Bowerman believed athletes needed a better track shoe than what was available and finalized the design of the Cortez in 1968. The shoe's initial name was "Mexico," referencing the 1968 Summer Olympics in Mexico City; after that, it was renamed "Aztec," but Adidas threatened legal action due to similarity with its Azteca Gold shoe. They then chose "Cortez," honoring Hernan Cortés, the Spanish Conquistador who led the expedition that ended the Aztec Empire. The shoe was introduced to the public at the peak of the 1972 Summer Olympics and gained widespread attention after U.S. Olympic athletes began wearing it. Sales reached $800,000 in the first year, a 100% increase over the 8,000 sales inquiries from the first year of selling Onitsuka Tiger shoes. The Cortez was initially made with leather, but Bowerman later switched to nylon and suede to reduce weight and improve comfort. The shoe features a simple design with the Nike swoosh on the sides and a streak on the lower sole, and its foam is generously placed to absorb road shock, reduce leg fatigue, and provide comfort, with one marathoner calling it "the most comfortable shoe ever." In 2009, the Cortez Fly Motion was released, incorporating flywire—lightweight Vectran threads—that further reduced the shoe's weight. The shoe has been redesigned multiple times and set an early standard for running shoes. It is also famously worn by George Costanza on Seinfeld and by Forrest Gump in the 1994 film Forrest Gump. The Nike Cortez is commonly worn by gangs in Los Angeles, notably MS-13; in January 2013, four Hispanic teenagers were shot in a Brentwood, California neighborhood after being asked why they were wearing Nike Cortez shoes, and all were injured. Nike eventually grew into a multi-billion dollar corporation operating in over 160 countries and employing more than 35,000 people. In 1974, Nike won a court battle to continue using the name "Cortez" after the shoe was previously known as the Onitsuka Tiger Cortez, and it was later renamed to the Onitsuka Tiger Corsair.
